step1_analysis.description: A 900-MHz CMOS cascode LNA with inductive source degeneration. The common-source transistor (XM1) provides gain and noise optimization, while the common-gate transistor (XM2) reduces the Miller effect and improves reverse isolation. XM2B is likely part of a bias mirror or ESD protection structure.

paper_reference.title: A Sub-1-dB NF 2.3-kV ESD-Protected 900-MHz CMOS LNA

power_consumption.description: Total DC power dissipated by the circuit from the supply.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted the gate bias to match the paper's target power consumption of 6 mW.

center_frequency.description: Frequency at which the voltage gain is maximized.

sky130_expected.calculation: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). With L=10nH and C=3pF, f = 918 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the LC tank components added in the testbench to match the paper's 920 MHz target.

voltage_gain.description: Maximum AC voltage gain at the center frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm = 2*Id/Vov = 36 mA/V. Gain ~ gm * Rload = 36m * 500 = 18 V/V = 25 dB. Taking into account input matching and parasitics, expect ~15-20 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the Q-factor of the load inductor and the chosen load resistor.

noise_figure.description: Signal-to-noise ratio degradation from input to output.

sky130_expected.calculation: NF is dominated by the input transistor's channel noise and induced gate noise. Sky130 0.15um devices typically achieve 1.5-2.5 dB NF at 900 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Modern short-channel devices have higher excess noise factors (gamma) than long-channel devices, making sub-1-dB challenging without very large devices and high-Q inductors.

input_return_loss.description: S11 parameter, measuring how well the input is matched to 50 ohms.

sky130_expected.calculation: Zin = s*Ls + 1/(s*Cgs) + gm*Ls/Cgs. With Ls=1nH, Cgs~100fF, gm=36m, Re(Zin) ~ 360 ohms. Matching will be poor without further tuning.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Requires precise co-design of Ls, Lg, and device width to achieve deep matching.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, and center frequency of the LNA.
step3_testbench.spice:
* 900-MHz CMOS LNA Testbench
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* Define parameters for realistic LNA sizing (overriding original small sizes)
.param W_xm1=100u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2b=10u L_xm2b=0.15u
.param W_xm2=100u L_xm2=0.15u

* DUT
XM1 N5 N2 N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2B VDD VDD N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2b} w={W_xm2b}
XM2 RFOUT VDD N5 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Biasing and Supply
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VBIAS N_BIAS 0 0.6
RBIAS N_BIAS N2 10k

* Source degeneration inductor
LS N6 0 1nH

* Load tank (10nH and 3pF -> ~918 MHz)
LD VDD RFOUT 10nH
CL RFOUT 0 3pF
RL RFOUT VDD 500

* RF Input with 50-ohm source
VAC IN_SRC 0 dc 0 ac 1
RS IN_SRC IN 50
CIN IN N2 10pF

.control
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

ac dec 100 100MEG 5G
let gain_db = vdb(RFOUT) - vdb(IN)
meas ac gain_at_920M find gain_db at=920MEG
meas ac max_gain max gain_db
.endc
.end
